title: Lion Brewery Co Returns to India After Six Decades With Premium Beer Launch
excerpt: The 1836-founded London brewery that helped pioneer India Pale Ale is entering Delhi's premium beer market with Copperdrop Spirits as its distribution partner.
body:
• Lion Brewery Co, originally founded in London in 1836, is re-entering the Indian market in July 2026 with its Island Lager and Pale Ale in 330ml bottles
  • The brewery — revived in Singapore in 2018 — is partnering with Copperdrop Spirits for India distribution, starting with Delhi before a planned national rollout
  • India's beer market, valued at roughly $4.5 billion in 2023, is projected to grow at 8–10% annually through 2028, with premium brands gaining ground fastest

Lion Brewery Co, a London and Singapore-based brewery originally founded on the banks of the River Thames in 1836, has announced its return to the Indian market after more than six decades. The launch, set for July 2026, will begin in Delhi with two products — Island Lager and Pale Ale — available in 330ml bottles and positioned squarely in the premium segment.

The move is not just commercial expansion. Lion Brewery Co was among the earliest producers and shippers of India Pale Ale, the beer style developed in Britain specifically for export to India during the colonial era. IPA's hop-forward, higher-alcohol character was born of necessity: the beer had to survive months at sea without spoiling. Lion's ales making the journey to Indian ports in the 1800s were part of that original trade, according to Aabkari Times.

"India is not just a new market for us — it's part of Lion Brewery Co's story. To bring Lion back after more than half a century, and to do so at a time when the premium beer segment is growing so rapidly in India, is incredibly exciting."

— Will Julius, Co-Founder and Managing Director, Lion Brewery Co

A Brewery Demolished, Then Reborn

The original Lion Brewery on the Thames was demolished in 1949, though Britain's King George VI requested that its iconic lion statues be preserved — they still stand in London today. The brand remained dormant for nearly seven decades until 2018, when a group of friends from Singapore and London revived it. The brewery now operates a flagship taproom and brewpub in Singapore's CBD, in a heritage building on Club Street, and sells across six countries on three continents.

Lion Brewery Co's brewing philosophy centres on sessionable beers — lower in alcohol but full-flavoured, bridging the gap between craft and commercial lagers. "People love to drink delicious, easy-going beers," Julius told Asia Food Journal. "They don't necessarily want to be knocked off their feet with an 8% ABV Double or Triple IPA."

Why Delhi, Why Now

India's beer market has reached a scale that premium international brands can no longer ignore. Valued at approximately $4.5 billion in 2023, it is projected to grow at a compound annual rate of 8–10% through 2028, with the premium and super-premium segments outpacing the broader market. Rising disposable incomes, rapid urbanisation, and shifting preferences among younger urban drinkers are driving demand away from mainstream lager toward imported and craft options.

Delhi, as one of India's largest premium beer markets, is the natural beachhead. The city's beer landscape is also in flux: a Mint investigation found that major brands like Kingfisher, Budweiser, and Heineken have all but disappeared from many state-run liquor stores since Delhi's 2022 excise policy reversal, with shelf space now occupied by lesser-known regional and imported brands. For a new premium entrant, the disruption could represent opportunity.

Distribution will be handled by Copperdrop Spirits, promoted by the founder of Bad Monkey Beer, a fast-growing premium brand in India. Brand strategy and market positioning are being shaped by Bev Connect, a consultancy founded by Madhavi Mohindra.

"We see strong potential for premium international craft brands in India. Lion Brewery Co combines heritage, authenticity, and quality — all of which resonate strongly with today's Indian consumer."

— Rohan Ratan Khare, Copperdrop Spirits

The Diaspora Connection

For Indians abroad — particularly in Singapore and the UK, where Lion Brewery Co already has a strong presence — the India launch closes a loop. The brand's taproom on Club Street in Singapore draws a significant South Asian crowd, and its beers are available across British pubs and bottle shops. Indians familiar with the brand overseas may now find it on home visits, while the historical IPA connection adds a layer of cultural resonance that few imported beers can claim.

What's Next

Lion Brewery Co plans to expand beyond Delhi into additional Indian cities following the initial launch, though it has not specified a timeline or target markets. The company's broader trajectory — from a kitchen startup in 2018 to six countries today — suggests ambition, but India's fragmented, state-regulated alcohol market is notoriously difficult for newcomers. Success in Delhi will likely determine the pace and scale of that national rollout.
